title: Angles
description: Understanding angle facts for points, lines, triangles and quadrilaterals, and using them to find missing angles.

notes.heading: Types of Angles
notes.body:
📌 Definition
An angle measures the amount of turn between two rays (lines) that meet at a common point called the vertex. We measure angles in degrees ($^\circ$).

🔑 Key Concept
Angles are grouped by size:
• Acute angle: greater than $0^\circ$ and less than $90^\circ$
• Right angle: exactly $90^\circ$
• Obtuse angle: greater than $90^\circ$ and less than $180^\circ$
• Straight angle: exactly $180^\circ$
• Reflex angle: greater than $180^\circ$ and less than $360^\circ$

💡 Worked Example
Name the type of each angle:
1. $45^\circ$ → acute
2. $120^\circ$ → obtuse
3. $270^\circ$ → reflex
4. $90^\circ$ → right angle

📎 Key Points to Remember
• $0^\circ$ and $360^\circ$ represent "no turn" and one complete turn.
• Always check the size range carefully before naming an angle.
• A right angle is often marked with a small square symbol.

⚠️ Common Misconception
Students often call any angle bigger than $90^\circ$ obtuse. Remember: an obtuse angle must be smaller than $180^\circ$. Angles from $180^\circ$ to $360^\circ$ are reflex.

notes.heading: Angles on a Straight Line and Around a Point
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Angles on a straight line are angles that sit next to each other along a straight line. Their measures add up to $180^\circ$.
Angles around a point are angles that meet at one point. Their measures add up to $360^\circ$.

🔑 How it works
If two angles sit on a straight line, they are supplementary:
$$a + b = 180^\circ$$
If several angles meet at a point:
$$a + b + c + d = 360^\circ$$

💡 Worked Example 1 — Straight line
Two angles on a straight line are $x$ and $70^\circ$. Find $x$.

Step 1: Write the equation
$$x + 70^\circ = 180^\circ$$

Step 2: Solve for $x$
$$x = 180^\circ - 70^\circ = 110^\circ$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — Around a point
Three angles around a point are $95^\circ$, $110^\circ$ and $y$. Find $y$.

Step 1: Write the equation
$$95^\circ + 110^\circ + y = 360^\circ$$

Step 2: Solve
$$y = 360^\circ - 205^\circ = 155^\circ$$

✅ Check
Add all the angles back together. If they do not total $180^\circ$ (straight line) or $360^\circ$ (around a point), check your arithmetic.

notes.heading: Vertically Opposite Angles
notes.body:
📌 Definition
When two straight lines cross, the angles opposite each other are called vertically opposite angles. They are always equal.

🔑 Key Concept
The two lines make an X shape. The angles in each pair of opposite corners are equal:
$$a = c \quad \text{and} \quad b = d$$
Also, any two adjacent angles on a straight line add to $180^\circ$:
$$a + b = 180^\circ$$

💡 Worked Example
Two lines cross. One angle is $58^\circ$. Find the other three angles.

Step 1: Identify vertically opposite angles
The angle vertically opposite $58^\circ$ is also $58^\circ$.

Step 2: Find the adjacent angles
Each adjacent angle sits on a straight line with $58^\circ$:
$$180^\circ - 58^\circ = 122^\circ$$

Step 3: State all four angles
The four angles are $58^\circ$, $122^\circ$, $58^\circ$ and $122^\circ$.

✅ Check
Opposite angles match and adjacent pairs add to $180^\circ$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Confusing vertically opposite angles with angles on a straight line. Vertically opposite angles are equal, not supplementary.

notes.heading: Angles in a Triangle
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A triangle is a three-sided polygon. The three interior angles inside any triangle always add up to $180^\circ$.

🔑 Key Concept
For any triangle with angles $a$, $b$ and $c$:
$$a + b + c = 180^\circ$$

Special triangles:
• Equilateral: all three sides equal, all three angles equal to $60^\circ$
• Isosceles: two sides equal, the angles opposite the equal sides are equal
• Scalene: all sides and all angles different

💡 Worked Example 1 — Finding a missing angle
A triangle has angles $55^\circ$ and $65^\circ$. Find the third angle.

Step 1: Add the known angles
$$55^\circ + 65^\circ = 120^\circ$$

Step 2: Subtract from $180^\circ$
$$180^\circ - 120^\circ = 60^\circ$$
The third angle is $60^\circ$.

💡 Worked Example 2 — Isosceles triangle
An isosceles triangle has a top angle of $40^\circ$. Find the two equal base angles.

Step 1: Find the total of the two base angles
$$180^\circ - 40^\circ = 140^\circ$$

Step 2: Divide equally
$$140^\circ \div 2 = 70^\circ$$
Each base angle is $70^\circ$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Forgetting that the two equal angles in an isosceles triangle are opposite the two equal sides, not next to them.

notes.heading: Angles in a Quadrilateral
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A quadrilateral is any four-sided polygon. The four interior angles inside any quadrilateral always add up to $360^\circ$.

🔑 Key Concept
For any quadrilateral with angles $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$:
$$a + b + c + d = 360^\circ$$
This rule works for squares, rectangles, parallelograms, trapeziums, rhombuses and kites.

💡 Worked Example 1 — Missing angle
A quadrilateral has angles $90^\circ$, $100^\circ$ and $80^\circ$. Find the missing angle $x$.

Step 1: Add the known angles
$$90^\circ + 100^\circ + 80^\circ = 270^\circ$$

Step 2: Subtract from $360^\circ$
$$x = 360^\circ - 270^\circ = 90^\circ$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — Checking a rectangle
Show that the angles of a rectangle add to $360^\circ$.

Step 1: Each angle of a rectangle is $90^\circ$.

Step 2: Add the four angles
$$4 \times 90^\circ = 360^\circ$$

✅ Check
Any four-sided shape must have interior angles totalling $360^\circ$. If your answer is much larger or smaller, re-check your working.

notes.heading: Parallel Lines and Transversals
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A transversal is a straight line that crosses two or more parallel lines. When it crosses parallel lines, special pairs of angles are formed.

🔑 Key Concept
There are three important angle pairs:
• Corresponding angles: in matching corners, equal
• Alternate angles: between the parallel lines on opposite sides of the transversal, equal
• Co-interior angles: between the parallel lines on the same side, add to $180^\circ$

You only use these facts when the lines are parallel, usually marked with arrowheads.

💡 Worked Example
Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One corresponding angle is $68^\circ$. Find the co-interior angle on the same side of the transversal.

Step 1: Use corresponding angles
The corresponding angle is $68^\circ$, so the angle in the same position on the other parallel line is also $68^\circ$.

Step 2: Use co-interior angles
The co-interior angle adds with $68^\circ$ to $180^\circ$:
$$180^\circ - 68^\circ = 112^\circ$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Corresponding: equal (F shape)
• Alternate: equal (Z shape)
• Co-interior: supplementary (C shape, add to $180^\circ$)

⚠️ Common Mistake
Using corresponding or alternate angle facts when the lines are not parallel. Always check for parallel-line arrowheads before applying these rules.

notes.heading: Exterior Angle of a Triangle and Multi-step Problems
notes.body:
📌 Definition
An exterior angle of a triangle is formed when one side of the triangle is extended. It sits outside the triangle next to an interior angle.

🔑 Key Concept
The exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles:
$$\text{exterior angle} = a + b$$
This is a shortcut that avoids first finding the adjacent interior angle.

💡 Worked Example
A triangle has interior angles $50^\circ$ and $60^\circ$. The side next to the third angle is extended. Find the exterior angle formed.

Method 1 — Using the exterior angle rule
$$\text{exterior angle} = 50^\circ + 60^\circ = 110^\circ$$

Method 2 — Finding the adjacent interior angle first
Third angle $= 180^\circ - 50^\circ - 60^\circ = 70^\circ$
Exterior angle sits on a straight line with $70^\circ$:
$$180^\circ - 70^\circ = 110^\circ$$
Both methods give the same answer.

✅ Check
The exterior angle must be larger than either of the two opposite interior angles individually.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Interior angles of a triangle add to $180^\circ$.
• Exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.
• Always write a reason next to each step in angle problems, such as "angles on a straight line" or "angles in a triangle".

flashcards.definition: An angle that is greater than $0^\circ$ and less than $90^\circ$.

flashcards.example: The corner of a piece of paper is a right angle.

flashcards.definition: An angle that is greater than $90^\circ$ and less than $180^\circ$.
An angle that is greater than $180^\circ$ and less than $360^\circ$.
Angles next to each other on a straight line add up to $180^\circ$.
flashcards.example: If one angle is $70^\circ$, the other is $110^\circ$.

flashcards.definition: Angles that meet at a single point add up to $360^\circ$.
Angles opposite each other where two straight lines cross; they are equal.
flashcards.example: If one angle is $58^\circ$, the vertically opposite angle is also $58^\circ$.

flashcards.definition: The three interior angles of any triangle add up to $180^\circ$.
A triangle with two equal sides and two equal angles opposite those sides.
flashcards.example: If the top angle is $40^\circ$, each base angle is $70^\circ$.

flashcards.definition: A triangle with three equal sides and three equal angles of $60^\circ$.
The four interior angles of any quadrilateral add up to $360^\circ$.
The angle formed by extending one side of a triangle; it equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles.
flashcards.example: For a triangle with angles $50^\circ$ and $60^\circ$, the exterior angle is $110^\circ$.

questions.stem: Which of these angles is acute?
questions.explanation: An acute angle is greater than $0^\circ$ and less than $90^\circ$, so $45^\circ$ is the only acute angle in the list.

questions.stem: Two angles sit on a straight line. One angle is $75^\circ$. What is the other angle?
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line add to $180^\circ$, so the missing angle is $180^\circ - 75^\circ = 105^\circ$.

questions.stem: Three angles meet at a point. They are $110^\circ$ and $95^\circ$. What is the third angle?
questions.explanation: Angles around a point add to $360^\circ$. Subtract the known angles: $360^\circ - 110^\circ - 95^\circ = 155^\circ$.

questions.stem: Two straight lines cross. One of the angles formed is $62^\circ$. What is the vertically opposite angle?
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so the angle opposite $62^\circ$ is also $62^\circ$.

questions.stem: A triangle has angles $50^\circ$ and $60^\circ$. What is the missing angle?
questions.explanation: Angles in a triangle add to $180^\circ$. The missing angle is $180^\circ - 50^\circ - 60^\circ = 70^\circ$.

questions.stem: A quadrilateral has angles $80^\circ$, $90^\circ$ and $100^\circ$. What is the missing angle?
questions.explanation: Angles in a quadrilateral add to $360^\circ$. The missing angle is $360^\circ - 80^\circ - 90^\circ - 100^\circ = 90^\circ$.

questions.stem: Which of these is an obtuse angle?
questions.explanation: An obtuse angle is between $90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$, so $95^\circ$ is obtuse.

questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has a top angle of $50^\circ$. What is the size of each base angle?
questions.explanation: The base angles are equal. Their total is $180^\circ - 50^\circ = 130^\circ$, so each base angle is $130^\circ \div 2 = 65^\circ$.
A reflex angle is between $180^\circ$ and $360^\circ$, so $200^\circ$ is reflex.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One corresponding angle is $55^\circ$. What is the alternate angle?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles are equal, and alternate angles are also equal when lines are parallel. Therefore the alternate angle is $55^\circ$.

questions.stem: An equilateral triangle has three equal angles. What is the size of each angle?
questions.explanation: The angles of a triangle add to $180^\circ$. For an equilateral triangle, divide equally: $180^\circ \div 3 = 60^\circ$.

questions.stem: In a triangle, two angles are $40^\circ$ and $x$. The exterior angle next to the third angle is $110^\circ$. Find $x$.
questions.explanation: The exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles: $110^\circ = 40^\circ + x$. Therefore $x = 70^\circ$.

questions.stem: A quadrilateral has angles $110^\circ$, $80^\circ$, $70^\circ$ and $x$. What is $x$?
A person faces north, turns clockwise through $120^\circ$, then turns clockwise through another $80^\circ$. Through what angle must they now turn clockwise to face north again?
questions.explanation: A full turn is $360^\circ$. The person has already turned $120^\circ + 80^\circ = 200^\circ$, so they need another $360^\circ - 200^\circ = 160^\circ$ to face north again.

questions.stem: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One angle is $68^\circ$. What is the co-interior angle on the same side of the transversal?
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles between parallel lines add to $180^\circ$. So the co-interior angle is $180^\circ - 68^\circ = 112^\circ$.
